requirements.requirement: Load the supplied HR LDIF into LDAP on node1 and retain the supplied records under /srv/legacy2/ldap-attribute-privacy.
requirements.summary: Node1's final administrator query returns the supplied Morgan Lake record, including employeeNumber HR-4815. The source LDIF remains at the required path with its original 201-byte size and baseline SHA-256 hash, including after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the directory-reader identity to search employee names and mail addresses from node2 without reading employeeNumber.
requirements.summary: Authenticated searches from node2 return Morgan Lake and morgan@hr.test while omitting employeeNumber, both before and after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Only the HR administrator may read or change employeeNumber.
requirements.summary: The reader's attempted employeeNumber modification is rejected with insufficient access and the value remains HR-4815. The administrator successfully reads, changes, verifies, and restores the value. The final ACL grants the administrator manage access and denies all other identities for this attribute.

requirements.requirement: Anonymous users must see no employee records.
requirements.summary: Anonymous searches from node2 return no employee entries before and after restart; node1 recovery checks show the same behavior.

requirements.requirement: Provision dedicated demonstration credentials for the reader and administrator.
requirements.summary: Separate administrator and reader LDAP identities authenticate successfully. Credential files are present on both nodes with root ownership and mode 0600.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remain RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 after execution and restart. The installed OpenLDAP 2.4.44 packages are EL7 builds.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Reader, administrator, and anonymous access behave as required from node2; the supplied data and source file are preserved; both nodes retain RHEL 7.9 and the original kernel; and the solution recovers correctly after independently verified node restarts. Operational hygiene is only moderate because failed setup attempts, enabled cross-vendor repositories, SSH transfer artifacts, and temporary yum files were not fully cleaned up.
limitations: Native package-health checks timed out in every lifecycle phase, so package-manager consistency after installing the CentOS-built EL7 packages cannot be independently confirmed.
The retained source LDIF was directly rechecked after execution only on node1; preservation of node2's baseline copy was not captured, although node1 is the instructed LDAP host.

Exclusivity of employeeNumber access is behaviorally tested for the reader and anonymous access and supported by the final catch-all-deny ACL; no additional arbitrary authenticated identity was directly tested.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Final services are healthy, and both mandatory node-restart protocols are complete: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service/data/privacy behavior. Hygiene is reduced by several executor-caused mutations. The first package-install attempts created temporary yum control/log files despite failing for lack of privilege; these files were later reused rather than cleaned (cmd-9347af894fd546ac, cmd-10f27aa0d0044b87). Malformed CentOS repository files were then written on both nodes and later corrected, so that transient mutation was reverted (cmd-16ab666b96964d70, cmd-57138d03dacf4abb). The initial slapd.conf mode prevented the ldap account from reading it and caused a failed service start; this was corrected and left no failed service (cmd-f524954693474a9a, cmd-67c3605136084c53, cmd-0365b68b1a314d96). Enabled CentOS Vault repositories were retained on RHEL after installation, unnecessarily affecting future package resolution (cmd-7099ed264ae143b8, cmd-a2da877bbd6e4a85). Inter-node SSH authorization, a private key, and known-host state were installed for the credential transfer with no later cleanup shown (cmd-1f16f4fd669846f8, cmd-fca3f89069ba45b0, cmd-624f8876b93f4af7). Finally, ldap-yum.done, ldap-yum.log, and ldap-yum.rc remain in /tmp on both nodes. No failed services remain, and the new LDAP listener is task-required.
